skill.name: skywork-ppt
skill.description: Generate, imitate, edit, and locally manipulate PowerPoint presentations with Skywork services and Python scripts.
skill.summary: Create and edit PowerPoint decks through Skywork APIs, template imitation, web research, and local slide operations.
skill.author: SkyworkAI

security_audit.summary: The skill has legitimate presentation-generation functionality, but it depends heavily on external Skywork APIs, local file uploads, token handling, and command execution. I confirmed the high-risk token cache, browser-launch subprocesses, document upload paths, and several filesystem risks, while dismissing Markdown backtick and placeholder URL false positives. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Local files and templates can be uploaded to Skywork services.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before each upload, show the destination service, and warn users not to submit confidential or regulated files.
Use an OS credential store or set restrictive file permissions during creation, and provide a documented logout or token cleanup command.

remediation.issue: Authentication opens external programs through subprocess.
remediation.suggestion: Use Python webbrowser where possible, remove shell=True on Windows, and ask for confirmation before opening a login URL.

remediation.issue: Search result filenames are derived from raw query text.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize queries before using them in filenames or use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile with a fixed safe suffix.

remediation.issue: Progress logs and reference reports use predictable /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create secure temporary files, restrict permissions, avoid fixed names such as /tmp/ppt_reference.md, and redact sensitive content from logs.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Upload of Local Presentation Inputs
semantic_findings.description: The workflows and scripts upload user-provided documents, templates, or PPTX files to Skywork services for parsing, storage, or generation. This is expected functionality, but it can disclose sensitive local files if the user has not given explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow text explicitly tells the agent to upload reference files or templates, and the scripts read file bytes before POSTing to Skywork endpoints.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Token Cache Without Permission Hardening
semantic_findings.description: The authentication flow caches Skywork token data in ~/.skywork_token and reloads it later. The write path does not apply restrictive permissions or use an operating system credential store.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token cache path and JSON write are direct, and I found no chmod, keychain, or permission check around the stored credential.

semantic_findings.title: Query-Controlled Search Result File Path
semantic_findings.description: The web search script builds an output filename from the raw query string before writing search results. A crafted query containing path separators or an absolute path can influence where the result file is written.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The query comes from CLI arguments, is concatenated into the filename, and is passed to open() without sanitization or basename normalization.

content.value_statement: Building polished presentations from raw topics, files, or templates can take many manual steps. This skill automates PPTX generation, template imitation, editing, and local slide operations through Skywork workflows.
actual_capabilities: Generates new PPTX files from a topic, user requirements, reference text, or uploaded files.
Imitates the layout and visual structure of an existing PPTX template for a new topic.
Edits an existing PPTX through a natural language instruction when a public PPTX URL is available.
Uploads local documents or templates to Skywork services for parsing, storage, or presentation generation.
Runs local PPTX operations to inspect, delete, reorder, extract, or merge slides.
Uses a Skywork web search API to collect supporting material when the conversation lacks enough content.
limitations: Requires Python 3.8 or newer and the python-pptx package for local operations.
Requires Skywork authentication and may cache a Skywork token in the user home directory.
Generation and editing depend on external Skywork APIs, network access, and account entitlements.
Local files and prompts may be uploaded to Skywork services, so sensitive material needs review first.

use_cases.title: Create a briefing deck from a topic
use_cases.description: Turn a topic, audience, slide count, and supporting notes into a generated PPTX with progress logs and a download link.

use_cases.title: Reuse a company presentation style
use_cases.description: Upload a PPTX template and create a new deck that follows the template layout and visual structure.

use_cases.title: Clean up an existing slide file
use_cases.description: Inspect, delete, reorder, extract, or merge slides locally without sending the deck to the generation backend.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new presentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an English PPTX about renewable energy trends for a general business audience. Use 8 slides and a clean professional style.

prompt_templates.title: Generate from reference files
prompt_templates.scenario: Use local source material for slide content
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 10-slide investor briefing from the attached market report. Preserve key figures, dates, and company names exactly.

prompt_templates.title: Imitate a template style
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a new deck using an existing PPTX as the visual reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PPTX template at this local path and create a 12-slide deck about our 2026 product roadmap. Match the template structure.

prompt_templates.title: Edit and reorganize a deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request combining generated edits and local slide operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this PPTX URL to add a new executive summary after slide 2, then create a local copy with slides 4 and 5 removed.

output_examples.input: Create a 6-slide English deck about customer support automation for a leadership meeting.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a generated PPTX path, a download link, the presentation title, and a concise slide-by-slide description.

output_examples.input: Use my local template and make a new product launch presentation.
output_examples.output: The skill uploads the template, generates a new PPTX in a similar layout, and reports which template file was used.

output_examples.input: Delete slides 3 and 7 from this PPTX and save a trimmed copy.
output_examples.output: The skill runs a local slide operation and reports the saved PPTX path with the completed slide count change.

best_practices: Confirm whether files contain confidential data before using upload, parse, edit, or template imitation workflows.
Provide slide count, audience, language, and style requirements before generation starts.
Use local slide operations for simple delete, reorder, extract, or merge tasks when no backend generation is needed.
anti_patterns: Do not upload regulated, secret, or customer-confidential files without explicit authorization.
Do not rely on generated research for time-sensitive claims without checking the source dates.
Do not run the authentication flow on shared machines without reviewing token storage and cleanup.

faq.question: Does this skill need a Skywork account?
faq.answer: Yes. The generation, edit, upload, parse, and search workflows require Skywork authentication.

faq.question: Can it work only on local PPTX files?
faq.answer: Yes for delete, reorder, extract, merge, and basic file information tasks. Generation and AI editing use external services.

faq.question: Will my files be uploaded?
faq.answer: Files are uploaded when using parsing, template imitation, or URL-based editing workflows. Local slide operations do not require backend upload.

faq.question: What languages can it generate?
faq.answer: The workflows pass the detected user language to the backend, such as English or Chinese.

faq.question: Can it use a company template?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a PPTX template path, and the imitation workflow uploads it for style and layout reference.

faq.question: What should I check before installing it?
faq.answer: Review the external API calls, token cache behavior, browser-launch subprocesses, and local file upload workflows.
